messages:
maya: Heads up — profiler shows a spike in PP bubble time after yesterday's schedule change. 1F1B runs have longer idle gaps on rank 2 and 3, looks like all-reduce waits pile up when microbatch=2

sam: Ugh. Any chance KV cache interactions are forcing extra synchronization? saw similar once when eviction path hit during decode

ravi: I pulled a perf trace. main culprit seems NCCL all-reduce latency variance + uneven microbatch distribution. attaching snippet from trace: 
```
rank2: wait_allreduce 12.4ms
rank3: wait_allreduce 17.9ms
compute: 8.6ms
bubble: 22.1ms
```

maya: thanks. also noticed a small regression after the kernel selector change (commit 7a2f9). selector picks int8-fused kernels for attn in some layers which increase compute but also change launch patterns

priya: can we try: microbatch=1, enable comm_compute_overlap=true, and fall back to fp16 kernels on last 2 layers? quick A/B to isolate

alex: started a 4-GPU run with those flags: 
`./run_infer --pp-sched 1f1b --microbatch 1 --comm-overlap true --kernel-policy conservative`

perf-bot: regression-alert: pp-bubble-avg increased from 11.3ms -> 18.7ms on the nightly cluster (4-GPU, seq_len=1024) :warning:

sam: hmm. with microbatch=1 bubbles should shrink but if all-reduce variance is high comm overlap won't help. maybe we need better tensor parallel balancing too

ravi: suggestion: add dynamic chunking for all-reduce (split into 2 chunks for heavy ranks) and let NCCL use asynchronous streams. Also try forcing smaller collective size: `NCCL_ALGO=Ring` vs `Tree` for our hw

maya: I ran an experiment: enabling async-allreduce + comm overlap + kernel-policy conservative dropped bubble from 22ms -> 12ms for seq=512, microbatch=1. but seq=1024 still shows spikes on rank3

priya: could be memory bus contention on GPU3 — it hosts largest layers in our TP mapping. try remapping tensors across TP to even compute. also check KV cache prefetch pattern: if prefetch touches same GPU repeatedly it creates hotspots

ravi: noted. I'll run a sweep: {microbatch: [1,2,4], comm_overlap: [true,false], kernel_policy: [aggressive,conservative], tp_map: [orig,swap-2-3]} and collect traces

maya: thanks — if we find a microbatch tradeoff that keeps bubble <13ms at seq1024 we can revert the selector change with a config toggle. prefer quick mitigation over big refactor

alex: attaching quick command for trace collection: 
```bash
NVPROF=1 REDWOOD_TRACE=1 ./run_infer --pp-sched 1f1b --microbatch 2 --seq_len 1024 --out trace_rank${RANK}.json
```

perf-bot: perf-run-complete: sweep run id sw-2026-03-17-09 flagged: best config microbatch=1, comm_overlap=true, kernel_policy=conservative, tp_map=swap-2-3 -> pp-bubble-avg 11.8ms

maya: perfect. Ravi — can you open a small rollback PR to gate the kernel selector behind a feature flag and add the tp remap as a temporary topology override? put perf numbers in the PR description

ravi: on it. will include flamegraphs and raw traces. estimated patch small, tests manual only for now

sam: once merged let's run a 24h soak on dedicated and watch tail latency (p95/p99)

maya: agreed. thanks everyone. we'll reconvene after soak. :thumbsup:
